problem: Suppose $A$ is a $5\times 5$ matrix and $det(A)=-15.$ The matrix $B$ is obtained from $A$ by applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{1}↔{R}_{5}$ (switching the first and the fifth rows). What is the value of $det(B)?$

activity_context.topic_title: Row and Column Operations on Determinants

feedback.problem: Suppose $A$ is a $5\times 5$ matrix and $det(A)=6.$ The matrix $B$ is obtained from $A$ by applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{1}↔{R}_{2}$ (switching the first and the second rows). What is the value of $det(B)?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since swapping any two rows changes the sign of the determinant to the opposite sign, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}det(B) & =-det(A) \\  & =-(6) \\  & =-6.\end{aligned}
$$
